title: Tiel-Coder ties Clef-Flash without thinking, *a short think passes it*
subtitle: The same 376 test items, one decision at a time. Callo reads the answer from the served model's own log-probabilities; its points are thinking budgets.

arms.name: flashnext-sharp
arms.label: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Sharp) · IQ3_XXS
arms.note: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (Sharp): ISTA-DASLab's GSQ-RCO IQ3_XXS GGUF in two shards (its GiB counts both; the n-gram shard is read lazily from SSD), served with the Sharp chat template v22.5.0; calibrated at budgets 0 and 256 only.
arms.gib_note: Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's counts both shards of its split GGUF, the n-gram shard read lazily from SSD

arms.name: gemma-e4b
arms.label: Gemma-4-E4B · UD-Q4_K_XL
arms.note: Gemma-4-E4B: budget 0 only (Callo cannot read its thinking format).

arms.name: clef-flash-bf16
arms.label: Clef-Flash 9B · BF16
arms.note: Clef-Flash 9B BF16: Cloudflare's checkpoint converted to GGUF at llama.cpp 1537a0a8 (native Clef path); the reference for every paired CI.

meta.timer: lat_ms = time.perf_counter() taken after the request body is serialised and immediately before a fresh http.client connection to 127.0.0.1 is opened and the request bytes are sent (loopback TCP connect included, as in kev's RemotePredictor and callo's own urllib timer), until the full response body is read and JSON-parsed. One request at a time, a fresh connection per request, no concurrency. The first --warmup records are sent once untimed and never written. The prompt render and tokenisation happen inside the server, so they are inside the wall (the analogue of callo's frame_ms + read_ms).

mean.subtitle: Tiel-Coder with no thinking matches Clef-Flash (−2.1 pp, CI includes 0) at 0.59× its mean latency, both on llama.cpp; ~140 thinking tokens put it +6.6 to +8.2 pp above Clef-Flash at 1.7–1.8 s mean.
mean.engines: Clef-Flash (release code): 574 ms mean, 2.0× the llama.cpp run's 286 ms; Tiel-Coder without thinking reads 0.29× against it, a gap of engines, not of models.

p50.subtitle: Tiel-Coder with no thinking matches Clef-Flash (−2.1 pp, CI includes 0) at 0.64× its p50 latency, both on llama.cpp; ~140 thinking tokens put it +6.6 to +8.2 pp above Clef-Flash at 1.4 s p50.
p50.engines: Clef-Flash (release code): 551 ms p50, 2.1× the llama.cpp run's 261 ms; Tiel-Coder without thinking reads 0.30× against it, a gap of engines, not of models.

p95.subtitle: Tiel-Coder with no thinking matches Clef-Flash (−2.1 pp, CI includes 0) at 0.55× its p95 latency, both on llama.cpp; ~140 thinking tokens put it +6.6 to +8.2 pp above Clef-Flash at 3.0–4.4 s p95.

mean.text: n = 376 test-s1 (mmlu 80, qnli 80, paws 80, composition_holdout 96, contrastive 40); idle M2 Ultra 64 GB, one at a time; Callo 2026-10-10 to 2026-10-13; Clef 2026-10-09; Kev-9B 2026-10-02.
Callo arms: --cache on (default); in-Callo frame + read wall time.
Client wall per request (clef_run.py: a fresh loopback connection, the round trip and JSON parse, one at a time).
In-process model forward only (kev.benchmark's LocalPredictor, MPS); tokenisation outside the timer.
Paired 95 % cluster-bootstrap CIs vs Clef-Flash (llama.cpp BF16), stratified by source; dashed line = its accuracy; tails run to each point's p95.
Callo's pick: the fastest point statistically tied with the most accurate (callo compare default, on mean).
Budgets are read from one generation per item, cut at each budget: an item that stops thinking early reads the same at larger budgets, so p50 and p95 can stack.

File size (GGUF; for native, safetensors shards and head, as shipped); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next's counts both shards of its split GGUF, the n-gram shard read lazily from SSD; Kev-9B's counts its base model.

Opt-in and experimental in Callo, never picked, so not plotted. At think 256, z .95 with the gate: Tiel-Coder 92.3 % at 1.0 s p50, from a separate calibration whose plain think 256 reads 92.3 % at 1.4 s p50 (the table's run: 92.0 %); Qwen3.8-Flash-Next 92.6 % at 2.1 s p50 (its plain think 256: 92.0 % at 5.5 s p50).
llama.cpp BF16 vs Clef-Flash's release code (2026-10-02 rows): 373/376 argmax agreement, median |Δp| 0.0006 (pre-registered bar 369/376 and 0.010: pass).
Clef-Flash (release code): 574 ms mean, 2.0× the llama.cpp run's 286 ms; Tiel-Coder without thinking reads 0.29× against it, a gap of engines, not of models.
